A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same STITCH research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable, and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations on reasoning and non-reasoning benchmarks, chunk-length sensitivity experiments, reasoning-augmentation experiments, and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds a human evaluation of perceived responsiveness, reported in Section 5 and Appendix D.

M1.justification: The STITCH-R/STITCH-S generation schedules, training-data construction, cross-entropy objective, backbone, and inference interventions are unchanged. Additional explanations do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: All training sources and benchmark tasks are retained. v2 adds a human-listener evaluation population, recruiting MTurk participants from the US, UK, Australia, and New Zealand to assess perceived responsiveness using existing GSM8K questions.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the matched benchmark and reasoning-augmentation experiments is unchanged. The new listener study compares existing STITCH variants, TBS, and the no-reasoning baseline; it introduces no new comparison method.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a distinct human-evaluation protocol: four model pairs, 100 GSM8K questions, three ratings per comparison, and a seven-point responsiveness scale. Initial silence simulates latency using profiled SLM processing and reported speech-synthesis latency. Existing benchmark protocols and training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 5 adds a completion-order analysis, comparing reasoning and response chunk counts and reporting no observed responses ending before reasoning finishes. Existing chunk-length sensitivity, external-reasoning experiments, qualitative cases, and unsuccessful training variants are retained, sometimes relocated.

E5.justification: v1 reports no formal significance tests or confidence intervals. v2 adds McNemar significance claims for the principal reasoning-versus-baseline comparisons and a 95% confidence interval for one human responsiveness comparison. Neither version reports repeated-training-run or seed-based uncertainty.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantive human responsiveness results in Table 6: STITCH-R versus TBS scores 1.164, STITCH-S versus TBS 1.687, STITCH-R versus STITCH-S -0.850, and STITCH-S versus no-reasoning 0.290. Existing benchmark scores, token counts, quality scores, transcription results, and Figure 3 curves are unchanged; these are new outcomes, not improved same-setting scores.

T1.justification: The sequence definitions, timing conditions, and latency calculations are retained. New Figure 5 illustrates the existing parallel-synthesis argument and its synthesis-time condition; it adds no theorem, proof, or mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same novelty, simultaneous-thinking-and-speaking, latency, and accuracy claims. The conclusion is shortened, but the omitted summaries of chunk-length control and external reasoning remain supported and stated in the body.

C2.justification: v2 attributes reasoning finishing before speech to the existing training-data filter and adds a tokenizer-access explanation for excluding Qwen-2.5-Omni fine-tuning. It also interprets the listener results as equal responsiveness for STITCH-S and no-reasoning, although the reported confidence interval excludes zero and does not establish equivalence.

D1.justification: Appendix B.2 adds a stated release and access link for the math evaluation audio. Appendix D documents listener recruitment, compensation, interface, and latency simulation. Existing training configurations, hardware, duration, data preparation, and prompts are retained; some disclosures move to the appendix.

R1.justification: v2 removes the Gemini native-audio reasoning discussion and Google citation, condenses audio-reasoning related work, and drops the MathArena and DeepSeekMath references. It adds two Qwen tokenizer-access references and P.808. Removing the Gemini discussion eliminates an explicit qualification of the novelty positioning.

P1.justification: v2 condenses related work and several explanatory passages, moves qualitative discussion ahead of the sensitivity experiments, and shortens the conclusion. It adds ethics and change-log sections and updates publication headers. Most existing prose and the main narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the human-results table, evaluation-interface screenshot, and two-panel synthesis-timing diagram. Figure 1 moves within the main text; Figure 3 and the STITCH-R example table move to the appendix. Existing plots and principal table designs are retained rather than substantially redrawn.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's timing arguments and automatic evaluations, v2 adds documented listener evidence supporting perceived responsiveness, statistical checks, and an evaluation-audio access link. These improve validation and reproducibility. The gains are limited by simulated onset delays, an unsupported equality interpretation despite a confidence interval excluding zero, and removal of the useful Gemini prior-work discussion.
